_readme: WORKED EXAMPLE — a backend service (here: a Python + SQL API). Shows the discover-then-reuse gates governing a NON-frontend codebase. The frontend block stays OFF. machinery.signals declares this project's own hand-roll shapes: writing raw SQL where the query-builder exists, re-implementing a serializer, etc. Adapt the regexes to your stack (Rust/Go/Java/Node all work the same way — you declare YOUR hand-roll shapes).

verification._readme: OFF here: this service has no app to drive, so neither the scripted-API gate nor an instrument roster has a subject. A backend that DOES have one (a CLI run under a harness, a container smoke run) declares it the same way — id / kind / driver / launch / receipt / enabled — and its receipts are read by the same reader.

rules.msg: print() is not observable in prod. Use the structured logger (acme.core.log).

specCatalog._readme: OFF here, but adoptable: nothing in this layer is frontend-specific (the class/`owns` half is gated on frontend.enabled). A Python project sets propReadRe to its own options shape (e.g. \b(?:opts|kwargs|cfg)\.([A-Za-z_]\w*)), emit to {callPrefix:'', decl:'', fnKeyword:'def', end:'', appendMethod:'append'}, and emitBans to the raw-assembly shapes its helpers exist to replace. See integrations/spec-catalog.md.
